title: Swin-UMamba: Mamba-Based UNet with ImageNet-Based Pretraining
mechanism: An ImageNet-pretrained VMamba (visual state space) encoder with a U-Net decoder inside the nnU-Net pipeline. Pretraining is what makes the Mamba U-Net beat CNN, ViT and from-scratch Mamba models.
adaptation: Average the 3-channel stem weights to 1 channel; 512 px (16 x 16 at the deepest stage). Use the PF fine-tune (frozen encoder 1k steps, then 0.1x lr), because the house fine-tune erases pretrained layers. Aim at E1, where half-cut layout and scuff streaks need cell-scale context. Needs the mamba-ssm CUDA build on cv02.
min_experiment: Swin-UMamba PF against house PF, 3 seeds each, 20k steps; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU, with test-49 crack IoU as a guard. Kill: under +0.03 E1 relF1@2, or test crack IoU worse by more than 0.01.
evidence: R: beats U-Mamba_Enc by 2.72% on average over AbdomenMRI, Endoscopy and Microscopy (2D). In U-Bench it ranks #3 zero-shot and #5 in-domain IoU over 28 2D datasets. In GP-VMxSMA it is on par with general-purpose models.
prior_overlap: The foundation-encoder screens (DINOv3/ConvNeXt linear probes, one 4k-step ConvNeXt-T PF fine-tune) did not test a pretrained SSM encoder under a full schedule, so this is open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Gray replicated to 3 channels, 512 px, 24 classes, label-safe aug, PF-style schedule (frozen encoder 1k steps, 0.1x lr) so the pretraining is not erased as in the house fine-tune.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Swin-UMamba (PF) v its scratch trainer v house PF, 5 folds. Metric: E1 relF1@2 and inactive IoU, CV crack relF1@2. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 over house PF.
